results.title: Kodak SlideTag Is a $35 Blind-Box E Ink Photo Display and AirTag Alternative | PetaPixel
results.content:
Reto, the company behind the wildly successful Kodak Charmera, has announced its next blind box-style product: the Kodak SlideTag. It’s a small, color E Ink display with AirTag-like capability and a user-replaceable battery.

The SlideTag uses that E Ink display to allow users to upload their own photos into it and display them like single slides from the golden age of film.

“When Kodak introduced Kodachrome in 1935, the slide mount quickly became the classic way people projected and shared their favorite memories. Families gathered around glowing projectors, watching their favorite moments illuminated inside a simple cardboard frame,” Reto says. [...] “Decades later, the Kodak SlideTag breathes new life into that iconic retro slide frame, bringing a vintage touch to the digital age. Designed as a miniature memory holder, it allows you to digitize your precious moments and easily carry your stories wherever you go.”

The SlideTag measures 39.3(W) x 46(H) x 7.58(D) mm and weighs just 16.6 grams. The central display is 1.54 inches across with a resolution of 240 x 240 pixels. The color E Ink can display up to six colors and because E Ink doesn’t require any power to retain the image, the SlideTag can display a photo and retain other functionality for extended lengths of time without dying. [...] The “other functionality” that does require battery power is the compatibility with Apple Find My and Google Android Find Hub. The IP54 rated keychain supports Bluetooth 5.4 and has a real-time tracking range of up to 30 meters while also being compatible with both Google and Apple’s tracking networks. The SlideTag can also buzz on command at 75 dB to help locate it.

# Hanging Film Slides on Your Bag? Kodak's New SlideTag Comes with Built-In Location Tracking

## Even portable location trackers are getting the vintage treatment~

## Summary

- Faithfully recreates the classic 1935 Kodachrome slide frame design, weighing just 16.6 grams to easily clip onto keys or bags.
- Features a 1.54-inch 6-color E-ink screen that can cycle through up to 12 photos offline, or switch to display to-do lists and QR codes.
- Supports both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub location networks, serving as an item tracker and luggage tag.
- Released as a collectible blind box with 8 vintage designs and 1 secret edition. [...] The small accessories clipped to bags or keys can offer more than just cute looks—they can be practical, too. Kodak recently introduced an electronic photo frame and tracker key fob called SlideTag. At first glance, it looks like a tiny vintage film slide, but the image inside changes to match your mood, all while housing built-in location tracking to prevent lost items.

The accessory draws inspiration from the classic Kodachrome color reversal paper slide mounts introduced by Kodak in 1935. SlideTag scales that familiar square paper frame down to a portable size, measuring just 39.3 × 46 × 7.58 mm and weighing around 16.6 g, making it lightweight enough to attach to keyrings, backpacks, or luggage handles without feeling bulky. [...] ### More than a mini electronic photo frame, it also doubles as a portable everyday tool

The front of SlideTag features a 1.54-inch 6-color E-ink screen, which official specs note delivers rich, detailed photo colors. Simply pair it via Bluetooth using the dedicated KODAK Memory Link App to upload shots from your phone’s photo library or snap a picture on the spot. The built-in storage holds up to 12 photos; once set to slideshow mode, the display automatically cycles through the images offline even when disconnected from your phone.

results.title: Kodak’s SlideTag is a Find Hub tracker that doubles as a tiny E-Ink photo frame - Android Authority
results.content:
Just as Amazon and other online retailers have started taking orders for Motorola’s unannounced Moto Tag 3, another brand is throwing its hat into the Bluetooth tracker ring. Reto Productions, the company behind the Kodak Charmera keychain camera, is launching its own take on the technology. This new tracker features a unique twist you won’t find on other trackers.

Called the Kodak SlideTag, the design is based on the iconic 1935 Kodachrome slide mount. In addition to working with both Google’s Find Hub and Apple’s Find My networks, it features a built-in six-color E-Ink display. This display measures 1.54 inches and offers a resolution of 240 x 240 pixels. [...] Through the Kodak Memory Link app, users can upload images directly from their gallery. The tracker has enough space for up to 12 photos, which can be shown in a looping slideshow format. You also have the option to display things like QR codes, to-do lists, calendars, countdowns, and more. According to the Amazon listing, the tracker has an average battery life of 12 months.

There are nine different retro designs, along with one special edition. As Reto is going with a blind box approach, which one you get will be a mystery. You can either buy a single box with one SlideTag or a whole set that contains eight blind boxes. There’s only a 1/64 chance that someone gets the special edition SlideTag. results.title: Kodak’s new SlideTag is a keychain tracker with a built-in E Ink photo display | DPReview
results.content:
The SlideTag comes from Reto, the Kodak brand licensee behind the viral Kodak Charmera and other retro-looking Kodak-branded products. Like those products, the SlideTag leans into the current nostalgia for old-school camera gear, and it’s styled to look like a 1935 Kodachrome slide mount.

Like the Charmera, the SlideTag is designed as a collectible. It comes in eight frame designs and is sold in blind boxes, so you don’t know which one you’ll get. Reto also made a rarer “secret edition” with a metallic finish, which has a 1-in-64 chance of turning up. You can buy the whole set, which still gives you a chance at the secret edition.

Kodak Slidetag keychain set featuring a branded product display box, two slide-shaped tags, a film strip, and a marketing brochure.Reto [...] In keeping with the collector theme, the package includes a “Kodak Memory Pocket” with a retro-style poster showing all the SlideTag versions, a mini film strip and a collectible Kodachrome slide frame.

Reto says the display is a 1.54-inch, 6-color E Ink screen with a resolution of 240 x 240 pixels. Images will look slightly pixelated and newspaper-like because of the e-paper technology, though that suits the retro look. E-paper also helps battery life, since it draws very little power.

A hand reaches for one of three square Kodak SlideTag labels, featuring printed photos of cats, a to-do list, and sunflowers.Reto [...] On the tracker side, the SlideTag works with both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub, and it has a 75 dB buzzer to help you find it. It supports Bluetooth 5.4, has a real-time tracking range of up to 30 meters (98 feet) and has an IP54 rating for some protection from the elements. It runs on a replaceable lithium coin cell battery.

You’ll need the free Kodak Memory Link app to upload images to the tracker. The display isn’t limited to photos, and it can also show to-do lists, countdowns, QR codes, contact details and more. A calendar function lets you schedule what to display in advance, and you can create a slideshow loop of up to 12 images.

The Kodak SlideTag is available now for $35 for a single box or $280 for the whole set.

results.title: Kodak SlideTag is an AirTag with an E-Ink display
results.content:
Offering support for iPhone and Android’s tracking networks, the new Kodak SlideTag offers the neat added functionality over an AirTag of being able to show your photos and more on an E-Ink display.

The Kodak SlideTag is inspired by classic 35mm slides from Kodak cameras, and is built by the same company, Reto, that launched a keychain digital camera inspired by old Kodak cameras too. The tracker’s E-Ink display is designed mainly to showcase your photos, with storage built-in for up to 12 photos, but also the ability to show lists and QR codes.

The SlideTag’s extra features are controlled by the Kodak Memory Link app, while tracking is handled in the Find My app on iPhone just like an AirTag (and the Find Hub app on Android phones). [...] There are nine total styles for the SlideTag, all sold in a blind box format. You can order one tracker for $35 with the whole set also available for purchase.

Eight of the styles have a one-in-eight chance of finding, while the ninth style is only found in one out of every 64 boxes.

Kodak SlideTag is available today from Amazon.
